correctness.rationale: Singleton factors force one selected position for each of q distinct letters. The factor c_{q-1}c_0 proves the necessity of avoiding the simultaneous endpoint selection. Each short nonwrapping factor is met by its chosen start letter; each short wrapping factor is met at an internal junction; for length >=q, all occurrences form a contiguous interval, and any one-per-letter selection outside that interval must use both endpoints. This proves the theorem for every q>=3,k>=2. The exact count is k^q-k^(q-2). Direct independent-of-proof factor-mask tests pass for 31 bounded (q,k) instances and 204695 selected position sets; those tests do not constitute an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result classifies ALL exact minimum covers of all factors for an unbounded family of finite words with independently variable alphabet size and repeat count, not just the minimum size. Its collapse of an exponentially large family of constraints to one special two-letter junction is a meaningful local-to-global rigidity, and k^(q-2)(k^2-1) gives the exact multiplicity relevant to position-based attractor studies. Unlike a binary special case or trivial bound, the proof controls q independent letter-position choices for arbitrary q>=3.
